newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 26.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 26.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:

** Telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd's (VSNL) successful jumbo issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) received 642 orders from investors in 28 countries, a source close to the deal says

Investment banking sources said U.S. institutional investors bought 33 percent of the issue. Funds in Britain picked up 30 percent of the issue with Asia contributing another 22 percent. The remaining 15 percent of the investment came from other parts of Europe and the Middle East.

** The State Bank of India (SBI) will review its prime lending rate (PLR) in April after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announces its six-month credit policy, chairman P.G. Kakodkar was quoted as saying
"We think the right time to take a decision on the PLR would be after the RBI slack season credit policy is available," the United News of India (UNI) quoted Kakodkar as saying
** U.S.-based Raytheon threatens to pull out of a venture to build an international airport in Bangalore due to delays in the project, the Economic Times newspaper reports

** Reliance Infrastructure and Larsen & Toubro are among corporates likely to approach the National Highway Authority (NHAI) to form joint ventures (JVs) to execute commercially viable road projects in the country, the Economic Times says
** India's largest car maker Maruti Udyog Ltd says it expects 1996/97 (April-March) car output to total about 335,000 units. Maruti produced 276,000 cars in 1995/96
"This year ending on March 31, we will produce about 335,000 vehicles," R.C. Bhargava, managing director of Maruti Udyog Ltd, told Reuters by telephone
** Auto components maker MICO Ltd says its net profit in 1996 jumps to 599.9 million rupees from 525.8 million a year earlier

** Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India may consider removing a cap of 5.0 million on individual shares and 40 million on a gross position in the present carry forward system at its board meeting in New Delhi later today, the Financial Express newspaper says
** Aluminium maker Hindalco has raised its stake in group firm Indian Rayon to 8.7 percent from less than 4.0 percent, the Business Standard newspaper reports
** The Bombay Stock Exchange's top-30 share index finished 35.58 points, or 0.95 percent, higher at 3765.78 on Tuesday
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.92/93 against the dollar on Wednesday, compared to the previous close of 35.90/91, dealers said
